questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Social aspects and academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a difficult process, but Vrije University did a lot of webinars helping the process

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a whole introduction day with a lot of information, which was good - but not a lot of follow up, and some of the information we got did not appear on Canvas, so when we needed the information we could not find it

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student dorms with shared kitchens and/or shared bathrooms, as well as studios

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The shared kitchens were fine - a little old, but with the essentials

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is really close to uni and the atmosphere is really nice - it is best to live in the shared kitchens but private toilets

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to apply for courses for the first period from November to mid January. It was first come, first served, which would have worked out fine for me if I was allowed to apply with a letter from my home university indicating I would finish my bachelor degree in January instead of my bachelor diploma (as I had to do master courses, and I was not done with my bachelor degree at the time of registration). The information of the courses were easy to find, but not always fully representable as I had a course where the professor messaged me after I was registered telling me that I was not able to take the course, as it was not my study area, but reading the course description I would be able to do it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The assistance regarding courses I received was bad. I was going on my exchange on my first semester on my master, which means that I had to do master courses. Unfortunately, I had not received my bachelor diploma before after the deadline of course registration, which meant that Vrije University would not accept my registration for my master courses. I had sent a letter from Copenhagen University indicating that I would finish my bachelor degree, but Vrije did not accept this. I had to figure out a solution myself, and I did not receive a lot of help in this chaotic proces. This resulted in me not being able to take one of the courses I needed to take from Copenhagen University, and therefore I could finish all 30 ECTS, but had to take 24 ECTS. I was very frustrated that they did not do a conditioned registration (that I could register for master courses on the condition that I passed my bachelor), as this means that I have to take extra courses in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very, as I described above - I had to find 2 bachelor courses in the first period instead of the master courses I planned to do, which made my process very difficult and unfortunately prevented me to do the courses I had to do

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a lot of back up courses since the ones you plan to do might not be accepted

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to do a mix of master and bachelor courses as I was not allowed to do master courses in the first period as I described above

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Vrije I think they are more generalizing (since they have periods, so you need to go through a lot of curriculum on a short time) while UCPH is more in depth (because of the semester structure)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Stress and health, Leading organizational change, Cross cultural management and Thought leadership in business (and field methods and linguistic analysis)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cross cultural management was very interesting, and it was a plus to have a different background as an exchange student as it made the course more relevant

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to go to the doctor a couple of times, and the first time they did not accept my European Health card - therefore, I had to pay myself. This was unexpected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The living expenses were close to the ones I am used to in Copenhagen, so most of it was just as I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had an Erasmus student network that organized a lot of social things for us as well as trips. Besides that, there was a sports center with a lot of classes and a fitness center

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus student network was amazing in the beginning before you get your friends, so you can get to meet all the other exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bike around the city and explore the less touristy areas - and find a lot of the cute bars, there are many

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was harder than expected as I thought my home culture was more similar than it actually was

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Dutch people are happy to talk in class, so that is a good place to talk with locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The straight forwardness and lack of patience in the culture

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness towards others

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) You learn many cultures as there are many exchange students coming to Amsterdam - so it is a multicultural environment, where you can learn a lot, so this is an amazing opportunity
2) The period system can be stressful as the periods are shorter than usual
3) The student dorms are a little out of the city, but it is a very nice place with green areas and nice people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not that I can think off no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students and learning a lot about myself and different cultures

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To adapt to the culture, because I did not expect it to be so challenging

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
